- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.7) — model tends to overshoot, especially after spikes.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.3) — model is overly conservative, often missing upward momentum.
- Lagged corrections: if recent history shows strong upward trend, model often fails to fully capture the momentum in early forecast days.
- Mean reversion bias: model frequently overcorrects after sharp spikes, leading to premature downward moves.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to underestimating late-period volatility, especially when sentiment turns bullish mid-horizon.
- Avoid averaging recent lows — model often anchors too early, ignoring sentiment-driven reversals.
- Spike recovery: after a sharp price spike, model tends to overcorrect downward, missing the continuation of the trend.
